items.title: CarMax Cuts Jobs for Third Time in 12 Months Amid Soft Auto Market
items.summary: CarMax has cut 145 white-collar jobs, approximately 4% of its corporate staff, marking its third round of layoffs in a year. This move by the nation's largest used-car retailer is part of a turnaround strategy under CEO Keith Barr to boost sales and profitability amidst high prices and rising interest rates in the auto market.

items.title: Coca-Cola to spend $10B on US manufacturing by 2030
items.summary: Coca-Cola and its bottlers are set to invest $10 billion in U.S. manufacturing infrastructure by 2030 to meet increasing demand for its products. These investments will expand production, distribution, and office facilities across various states. The announcement follows a commissioned study revealing Coca-Cola's substantial economic impact in the U.S., contributing $85 billion to the GDP and supporting one million jobs.

items.title: Kroger Drops Red Bull, Some Boar's Head in Price Fight
items.summary: Kroger has removed Red Bull from all its stores and some Boar's Head products from approximately 200 locations due to disputes over proposed price increases. This move is part of CEO Greg Foran's strategy to enhance Kroger's competitiveness by focusing on lower prices and faster service amidst rising food costs and inflation. While Red Bull's removal was directly linked to price, Boar's Head disputed that price was the reason for its partial delisting, citing operational and strategic factors.

items.title: Microchip Rises 17% YTD: Should You Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
items.summary: Microchip Technology (MCHP) shares have risen 17.3% year-to-date, underperforming the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector. While the company benefits from strong demand in data centers, industrial, automotive, and aerospace/defense markets, it faces challenges such as supply chain constraints, elevated debt, and intense competition. The stock currently has a "Hold" rating from Zacks Investment Research due to its premium valuation and balanced risks.

items.title: East Coast bank to lay off dozens of workers, close Tempe facility
items.summary: Truist Bank, the retail banking arm of Truist Financial Corp., plans to close its Tempe, Arizona facility and lay off 120 employees. The layoffs, impacting workers in its near-prime auto loan subsidiary Regional Acceptance Corp., will occur in phases from November 30 through February 28, 2027, coinciding with the permanent closure of the facility. This decision was communicated to the Arizona Department of Economic Security in accordance with the WARN Act.

items.title: PG vs. CL: Which Consumer Staples Giant Has Stronger Market Position?
items.summary: This article compares the market positions of two consumer staples giants, Procter & Gamble (PG) and Colgate-Palmolive (CL). While PG boasts a broad portfolio and scale, Colgate's strength lies in its dominant oral care franchise and stronger operating momentum, as reflected in its recent stock performance and analyst estimates. The analysis concludes that Colgate currently presents a stronger investment case due to its healthier projected growth and increasing market confidence.

items.title: Edison International stock falls as wildfire costs threaten growth
items.summary: Edison International's stock has fallen, trading near its 52-week low, primarily due to ongoing concerns about wildfire liability in California and the failure of protective legislation. Despite beating EPS estimates in Q2 2026, the company experienced a revenue miss, highlighting the pressure from legal, insurance, and borrowing costs. The utility reaffirms long-term EPS growth targets, but its stock performance is heavily impacted by these unresolved financial risks.

items.title: PG&E announces new California microgrid grant awardees
items.summary: Pacific Gas and Electric Co. (PG&E) has awarded over $30 million in new grants for community microgrid solar projects across California, marking a significant expansion of its Microgrid Incentive Program. These projects, which build on an earlier $43 million investment, will enhance grid resilience in rural, coastal, Tribal, and high wildfire risk areas by using solar-plus-storage systems and innovative pumped-hydro designs. They aim to maintain power for critical facilities like hospitals and schools during outages and advance clean energy solutions.

items.title: Marshalls Is Closing Stores: See Updated List of Doomed Locations for 2026
items.summary: Marshalls is reevaluating its retail footprint across the U.S., leading to both permanent and temporary store closures, as well as relocations, while simultaneously expanding its operations. Its parent company, TJX, reported a 7 percent increase in net sales to over $60.4 billion last fiscal year and plans to accelerate store openings, aiming for a total of 7,500 stores globally. The closures are a strategic move to optimize locations for better long-term returns, rather than an indicator of declining health in the off-price retail sector.

items.title: KKR Launches Equipment Finance Platform Akrapoint Commercial Capital
items.summary: KKR has launched Akrapoint Commercial Capital, an equipment finance platform focused on vocational, specialty trailer, and industrial equipment financing for small and middle-market businesses. KKR's Asset Based Finance strategy will commit $350 million to support the launch. The new platform will be led by CEO Nate Smith and chaired by Gary Shivers, bringing together extensive industry experience and long-term capital to address growing demand for equipment financing.
